prompt: Why did so many medieval people use public bathhouses?

options.text: Because fetching and heating water for a tub at home was hard work
Because bathing at home was forbidden
Because only nobles were allowed to wash

explanation: With no plumbing, filling a tub was laborious; bathhouses did that work, and most towns had at least one.

prompt: How many bathhouses did Paris have in the late 13th century?
explanation: Sources give 26 bathhouses in 1292, or more than 32 in the 13th century.
misconception: The “thousand years without a bath” idea doesn’t match the records of medieval towns.

prompt: When did Europe’s public baths go into decline?

options.text: At the very start of the Middle Ages

explanation: The decline was rapid in the 16th century; by 1526, Erasmus said the baths of Brabant were gone.
